title: Seeds of the Word
hookLine: Justin Martyr said wisdom in pagan philosophers came from seeds of the Word

lines: AN OLD MAN BY THE SEA.
cards: A young man is shopping for a philosophy. One teacher wants to talk about fees before truth. Another tells him to master music and geometry first.

He settles on the Platonists, until one day, walking alone near the sea, he meets an old man who starts asking him questions he can't answer. The old man points him to the prophets and to Christ, then walks off.
A fire, he says later, was kindled in his soul. That's how Justin tells his own story. A new block starts today, the great thinkers, and Justin goes first.

teach.h: IN THE BEGINNING WAS THE WORD.
teach.b: Justin became a Christian, but he didn't throw away his philosopher's books. He kept a question: what about all the true things Plato and the others said?
His answer starts with the opening of John's Gospel: "In the beginning was the Word." In Greek, the Word is the Logos.

teach.h: THE LIGHT THAT LIGHTETH EVERY MAN.
teach.b: And John says of it: "That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world." So Justin reasoned that the Word had been sowing seeds long before anyone heard of Jesus.

In a defense addressed to the Roman authorities, he writes, roughly, that whatever has been rightly said among all people belongs to us Christians, and that the writers of the past saw truly by the seed of the Word planted in them.

He thought they saw in part, and that in Jesus the whole Word had come. But he would not call their wisdom worthless. There was a precedent, in the same speech at Athens this path heard two weeks ago.
There Paul quotes Greek poets to the crowd: "For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring." Justin paid for his faith.
Tradition says he died for it in Rome, which is why he's remembered as Justin Martyr. Christians still weigh his idea differently. Some find seeds of truth widely scattered.
Others stress more sharply what only Christ reveals. This path ranks neither. Justin's question can travel with anyone: when you hear something true, where did the seed come from?

how: Christian teachers since Justin have drawn on Greek philosophy to explain the faith; churches differ on how much truth they find in other philosophies and religions, and some Catholic teaching uses Justin's phrase "seeds of the Word".

games.q: what does “seeds of the word” mean?
o: Jesus' story of a farmer scattering his grain
the first Bible verses a child learns by heart
Justin's idea that God's Word sows truth everywhere

p: an old man by the sea

s: Justin thought the Greek philosophers said nothing true
he wrote that whatever was rightly said among all people belongs to Christians, seen by the seed of the Word.
Paul quotes Greek poets in a speech in Athens
"as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring."
Justin stopped being a philosopher when he became a Christian
in his own telling, he kept teaching, and treated the faith as the philosophy he had been looking for.

games.q: you're Justin, a Christian teacher who still loves Plato. a fellow believer says: throw out the philosophers. what do you do?
o: keep reading, and look for seeds of the Word.
keep Plato and the Gospel in rooms that never meet.
games.why: Justin reads the philosophers as people who saw in part, by seeds the Word had sown, while holding that in Jesus the whole Word had come.

practice: Bring to mind a person whose life looks very different from yours: different politics, a different faith or none, a different generation.
Look for one wise thing they've said or done, and without arguing with the rest of what they think, hold that one thing and turn it over, the way Justin read Plato.
If you pray, you can give thanks for the wisdom, wherever it came from.

wordCard.voice: Seeds of the Word. Justin's idea that the Word of God sows truth in people everywhere, so wisdom found anywhere can be honored.

orig.note: Greek: the seed-bearing Word, Justin's phrase for the Word sowing truth in every people.

carryVoice: Your line: seeds everywhere. Wisdom found anywhere, by anyone, can be honored. See you tomorrow.
